consensus_summary: Across the blind responses there is a settled primary consensus that the lost sheep symbolizes the sinner or spiritually straying person whom God/Christ the Shepherd actively seeks, finds, and joyfully restores; common secondary applications include the lost sheep of the house of Israel, backslidden disciples/church members, and related pastoral or prophetic extensions.
book_summary: The book identifies the lost sheep primarily as the scattered house of Israel mingled with the nations, sought and regathered, and more generally as any unrepentant sinner.
consensus_core_identification: A straying sinner (person or people) sought and restored by the divine Shepherd.
book_core_identification: Primarily the scattered house of Israel mingled with the nations (sought and regathered); secondarily any unrepentant sinner.
boundary_disagreement: The book elevates and further specifies the Israel reading (scattered/mingled with the nations, regathered) as the lead referent, treating the generic unrepentant sinner as the broader secondary sense; consensus treats the generic sinner as primary and the house-of-Israel sense as a common but secondary contextual application, with literal lost-tribes/mingled-nations readings rare or fringe.
material_contradiction: None on the shared image of straying and divine seeking/restoration; the disagreement is priority, precision, and ethno-historical extension rather than outright denial of the other referent.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on straying parties sought by God and both explicitly allow a general-sinner reading, so this is not a replacement of the central category (not DIVERGENT) nor absent from consensus alternatives (not NOVEL). The book preserves the category but materially narrows and re-ranks the primary extension toward scattered Israel mingled with the nations (with a regathering emphasis tied to its Israel/Ephraim frame), which is a boundary/precision change characteristic of REFINED rather than mere wording equivalence (MATCH).
strongest_objection: Consensus primary meaning is fixed by the Luke 15 / Matthew 18 parables on the repentant sinner and heavenly joy; leading with a scattered-mingled-Israel/regathering sense (and cross-reference into an Israel/Ephraim chapter) inverts that priority and risks importing a specialized lost-tribes extension that mainstream consensus marks as secondary or rare.
